note: Capabilities with no caller outside scripts/. See scripts/check-callers.ts and #72. This file may only SHRINK — the check fails when an entry becomes reachable and is not removed. 40 on 2026-09-16; app.mcp_expire_codes wired the same day; the three hq_*_tool wrappers, app.expire_temporary_staff and app.expire_undo_offers wired the same day under #272; app.autonomy_for wired by 0421 under #15 — the dial now decides something; public.project_artifacts wired as an hq-api section under #260. 0451 dropped public.hq_stranded_work and public.hq_eval_latest: the Governance page now reads both through app.hq_governance, so the separate wrappers were a second door to the same data. 31 -> 29 on 2026-09-17. 0452 dropped public.what_i_can_do (a second implementation of capabilityBrief, which builds every prompt) and public.hq_output_shapes (a mouth over a registry nothing reads); public.containers_stored_as_documents gained its caller in check:leaks. 29 -> 26 on 2026-09-17. check:callers learned that an OPERATOR COMMAND is a caller — a script an npm script runs, excluding verify:*, poc:* and the gate. Eight entries were reachable by a documented command Grant runs (eval, check:leaks, purge:fixtures, telegram:bots, inventory, slack:backfill) and were never dead. 26 -> 18 on 2026-09-17. 0454/0455 dropped the superseded task API: app.task_add is the live one the gateway and the Tasks tab use. Dropping the three wrappers PROVED app.project_tasks and app.set_task_state dead, which is why the wrappers went first. 18 -> 15 on 2026-09-17. 2026-09-17: app.needs_me_pressure removed — the morning briefing now says how many requests the needs_me cap is holding back and how long the oldest has waited (0469). Both were things nothing said: the cap hid the sixth request silently, and "past a real deadline" cannot see a request nobody dated. 15 -> 14. 2026-09-17: app.channel_for and app.slack_channels_for_project REMOVED (0470) — both read slack_channel_map and src/slack/provision.ts queries that table directly in six places for the columns each step needs, so the provisioner outgrew them. Wiring six working queries to call them would be the mechanical connection #272 forbids. 14 -> 12. public.awaiting_review wired as the `review` section under #276 — 0471 made it able to return a row at all. public.raise_proposals wired by the proposal-round duty under #49/#272 — 0473: nothing had ever turned an impediment into a proposal. 2026-09-18: app.proposals_sent and public.proposals_to_send left the baseline because the proposal round now calls them (0489). They were not dead code — they were #49's loop with its last link missing, so the office raised proposals correctly and never told Grant. That is what this check is for: the question is not 'is this function used' but 'is a real capability unreachable'. 2026-09-18, second pass: all eight survivors now carry a reason in `why`, which is what #272 asks for — the question is not 'is this function used' but 'is a real capability unreachable'. One of the eight, `app.suppress_delivery`, is the interesting answer: it is unreachable because the state it acts on never occurs, not because a caller was forgotten. An entry with no reason remains an admission rather than a decision. 2026-09-23, #351: check:callers was counting a mention inside a COMMENT as a call, on both sides — the database half read decide_suggestion's comment as a caller of raise_suggestions, and the repository half masked its own fix when a comment beside the new call named the function in prose. Stripping comments surfaced four functions that were always unreached and never visible: app.unarchive_document, public.model_speed, app.mail_recent, app.notebook_chat_allowed. They are recorded rather than fixed here, each with a reason. 8 -> 12, and this is the one direction this file is allowed to grow: the instrument got better, not the product worse. 2026-09-23, pass 27: app.notification_patterns' reason was FALSE and is corrected above -- the third false baselined reason this programme has found. A baselined reason is a claim about the product and must be checked like any other; a documented excuse is worse than a bare gap because it stops the next person looking. 2026-09-23: the four public.sign_in_* functions entered this baseline without being this branch's work. The ownership rule added under #351 skips a function no migration here names -- and copying the sibling branch's applied migration in, which npm run migrate requires, made them named. Each carries the branch it belongs to and whether a caller was verified there.

why.app.create_temporary_specialist: FOR THE OFFICE, not for Grant. It is the only route by which the application role may add staff, and #128's hand-off is what uses it when a job needs a specialist the roster has not got. Only `verify:agents` names it today because no real job has yet needed one — the absence is a fact about traffic, not a missing caller, and a button for it would be Grant hiring somebody to answer a question he has not asked.
why.app.notification_patterns: THE FEEDBACK LOOP'S LAST LINK, and this entry's previous reason was FALSE. It claimed `npm run levels` and the learning page answer the question a person asks. Neither names this function or public.notification_events: checked 2026-09-23 by grepping scripts/ and by asking pg_proc for any function whose definition mentions notification_patterns -- the only row returned is the function itself. It is the ONLY reader of notification_events.outcome, which is what a thumbs up or down on Telegram and Slack writes, so the reaction buttons terminate here. public.feedback, the other half of the same press, has no reader at all. Recorded rather than wired: public.feedback holds seven rows, every one positive, none since 6 September, and building learning over a table with no signal in it is the public.contacts trap. 0580 and 0581 removed the Settings cards' claims that a press is read. What a reaction should DO is filed, not guessed at here.
why.app.suppress_delivery: THE ARCHITECTURE DOES NOT HAVE THE WINDOW IT NEEDS. It stops a QUEUED message going out when an undo lands first. `public.deliveries` has only ever held `sent` and `failed` — the notifier writes the row at the moment it sends, so there is no interval in which a pending delivery exists to be suppressed. Reachable the day delivery becomes a queue; inventing a caller before then would be a control for a state that cannot occur.
why.app.teach_expertise: A SYNONYM. The Team page's expertise field (`data-f="p_skills"`) is the control Grant uses and it writes the same column through the staff writer. This is the ADDITIVE, de-duplicating version an agent or a script uses; a second control beside a working one would be furniture, which is the same judgement `action:revoke_tool` carries in the pressable baseline.
why.public.connector_sheet: REACHED ANOTHER WAY. The Connections tab renders capability sheets from the payload the page already fetches; this is the same answer shaped for an API caller.
why.public.delegation_health: AN OPERATOR MEASURE. `npm run measure` is the reader Grant has for whether delegation is real, and it is the one CLAUDE.md points at. This is the per-window detail behind it.
why.public.self_changes: AN OPERATOR MEASURE, and the Governance page already answers the question a person asks — what the office learned and why it changed (#54) — from the lessons and events readers. This is the raw ledger view.
why.public.skill_effect: AN OPERATOR MEASURE. Whether acquiring a skill changed anything is answered for a person by the learning page; this is the numbers behind it, used by `verify:acquire` and `verify:skills` to prove the claim.
why.app.unarchive_document: surfaced 2026-09-23 by #351: check:callers counted a MENTION INSIDE A COMMENT as a call, on both the database and the repository side. src/projects/sync.ts names it only in prose.
